# ESOPHAGITIS

Esophagitis is usually associated with non-infectious diseases like gastroesophageal reflux disease, mucositis, and pill-induced esophagitis. Esophageal infection occurs primarily in immunosuppressed individuals (e.g. chemotherapy, transplantation, HIV) and rarely in healthy individuals. Most of the infectious esophagitis is caused by Candida albicans, cytomegalovirus (CMV) and herpes simplex virus. Aphthous ulceration of the esophagus is common in HIV infection. HIV screening is recommended.
